<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>This study presents the first micro-wear analysis of stone tools made from volcanic rocks from the Olduvai Bed II FC East (FCE) and FC West (FCW) sites at Olduvai Gorge, Tanzania, dated to approximately 1.6–1.5 Ma. These sites form part of a key stratigraphic interval documenting major technological and biological transitions during the early Pleistocene. The analysed sample comprises 46 well-preserved artefacts selected from a larger assemblage of volcanic rocks. The methodological approach adopted in this study relied primarily on scanning electron microscope (SEM). Despite the age of the assemblage and the challenges posed by raw material variability, micro-wear was identified on several pieces, providing direct evidence of tool use. The distribution and morphology of traces indicate that most tools were employed in longitudinal motions and cutting actions, likely associated with butchery. A smaller subset of artefacts exhibits wear patterns consistent with scraping of medium-to-hard contact materials.</jats:p>

<jats:title>ABSTRACT</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Compound‐specific stable isotope analysis (CSIA) has been widely applied to modern and archaeological samples of animal and human body tissues to evaluate food habits and/or physiological conditions. However, these techniques have rarely been applied to aquatic mammals, for which further study is required to evaluate their utility. This study conducted compound‐specific carbon isotope analysis of several individual amino acids using high‐performance liquid chromatography for separation and purification. This approach was applied to hair samples from two aquatic mammal species, including an archived stuffed specimen, to infer the nutritional sources in their aquatic environments, demonstrating its potential for use with diverse specimen types.</jats:p>

items.abstract: Reconstructing the dietary and habitat preferences of extinct taxa is essential to understand the selective pressures that drive morphological and behavioral evolution, which provides a necessary framework for understanding macroevolutionary patterns and how extinct lineages navigated ecological shifts across time and space. This study examines the degree to which environmental changes influence dietary intake by analysing dental microwear in Heteroxerus rubricati , an extinct xerine squirrel from the Middle Miocene (Aragonian) of the Iberian Peninsula. We examined 85 upper molars from multiple sites across two environmentally distinct geographic regions in Spain (the Madrid Basin and the Calatayud-Montalbán Basin), during a time of significant climatic change coinciding with the Middle Miocene Climatic Transition (15.0-13.5 Ma). Four microwear variables (fine scratches, wide scratches, small pits, and large pits) were quantified to proxy the consumption of grasses, seeds/dust, nuts, and arthropods. Notwithstanding the consistency of a mostly granivorous diet in both locations, H. rubricati exhibited notable spatiotemporal shifts in microwear signatures. While the Madrid Basin sample exhibited a high frequency of small pits, correlating with elevated environmental aridity and the subsequent ingestion of exogenous dust, the Calatayud-Montalbán Basin sample also showed a greater importance of fine scratches and large pits, which correlate with a more mesic, forested habitat with a higher dietary component of grasses. Additionally, signal variation related to the consumption of grasses shows temporal changes in both basins associated with variations in the amount of herbaceous vegetation in the landscape during this time interval. Therefore, the dietary signal of H. rubricati was not static; rather, it suggests a high degree of dietary plasticity fundamentally governed by localised resource availability in response to external environmental controls. Notably, the correlation between small pits and arid conditions highlights the utility of microwear as a high-resolution proxy for paleoclimate. Ultimately, these findings underscore the role of environmental aridity as a primary macroevolutionary force, shaping the ecological niche and evolutionary trajectory of small mammal lineages by modulating the interaction between the organism and its available food resources.

items.abstract: <jats:p>In South Asia, the northern Vindhyan Plateau in central India preserves a rich Palaeolithic record derived from both alluvial plains and the Kaimur hill range. The Middle Son Valley (MSV), one of the key river basins in this region, has been extensively studied by various scholars and institutions, yielding a significant record of Palaeolithic sites along with vertebrate fossils from dated, stratified alluvial sediments. However, relatively little is known about the nature of Palaeolithic remains in the tributaries, neighbouring river valleys, and foothill zones of the Kaimur Range within the peripheral areas of the MSV. This research addresses this gap through systematic archaeological investigations carried out between 2012 and 2025 in the neighbouring regions of the MSV. Fieldwork involved structured surveys, documentation of lithic assemblages, and analysis of their geomorphological contexts. A total of 787 lithic artefacts were documented from surface sites and stratified localities, collected from sedimentary exposures and selected surface contexts. The investigations led to the discovery of several new Palaeolithic sites, prehistoric painted rock shelters, and related archaeological assemblages in the Kaimur hill range and its foothills, as well as in adjacent river valleys, often preserved within well-stratified deposits. The foothill zones yielded Acheulean assemblages dominated by cleavers from secure stratified layers, alongside artefacts attributable to the Late Palaeolithic or Mesolithic, mostly recovered from surface contexts. Additionally, hundreds of painted prehistoric rock shelters were documented in the Kaimur Range, associated with Late Palaeolithic or Mesolithic assemblages and other archaeological remains. In neighbouring river valleys - such as the Rihand, Mayar, Tons, Gopad, Ken, and Choti Mahanadi - numerous Lower, Middle, and Late Palaeolithic or Mesolithic artefacts were recorded, along with vertebrate fossils from stratified layers. These findings demonstrate that the peripheral zones of the MSV form a significant archaeological landscape that reflects recurrent hominin occupation. The results further suggest that the Vindhyan basin provided a favourable ecological setting for sustained Palaeolithic habitation and adaptation, offering new insights into the distribution and behavioural patterns of prehistoric populations across the wider Middle Son Valley region.</jats:p>

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Foraging strategy frequently drives morphological diversification in birds. The plunge‐diving behavior of certain species makes the functional and ecological trade‐offs of variation in cervical vertebrae an especially intriguing question. This study compares cervical vertebrae across five plunge‐diving species and two non‐plunge‐diving species, using morphometric analysis of micro‐CT scans to test whether diving birds share specialized cervical vertebrae morphologies distinct from non‐divers. Plunge‐divers repeatedly experience extreme impact forces during headfirst water entry, requiring the neck to function as a shock‐absorbing spring rather than a flexible manipulative system. To withstand these forces, plunge‐divers exhibit reinforced cervical vertebrae—short, wide vertebrae with expanded joints and thickened arches. These features help distribute compressive and bending loads and reduce stress on the spinal column during impact. Gannets and boobies, the most extreme plunge divers, have an additional articulating surface on the dorsal arch of their anterior cervical vertebrae which limits flexion in the beginning of the neck further reinforcing against high loads. Additionally, we see that all plunge‐diving sulids experience similar water impact durations and that the ratio between the radius of the head and the neck scales with impact velocity.</jats:p>
authors: Megan L. Vandenberg, Alissa Perez, John Michael Racy, Adam P. Summers, Ed Habtour, Bart Boom

<jats:title>ABSTRACT</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Lago Maggiore is situated in an overdeepened valley reach at the southern margin of the European Alps, and its thick sediment infill allows the reconstruction of the postglacial valley and lake evolution. We study here the sedimentary succession in the lower Ossola Valley, which is infilled by ~500 m of deposits. In a marginal position, a core of the International Continental Scientific Drilling Program (ICDP) recovered a 58‐m‐long sediment succession that is investigated by sedimentological and geotechnical analyses, luminescence and radiocarbon dating, and contextualised by reflection‐seismic data. The succession consists of a basal coarse‐grained interval that is overlain by ~35 m of silts and sands, reflecting an ice‐retreat sequence and the establishment of glaciolacustrine conditions. A distinct transition from homogeneous silt‐dominated to sandier, more heterogeneous lake deposits is attributed to a dam breach and lake‐level drop resulting in sudden delta progradation at ca. 9 ka. A clustering of mass movements in other Alpine lakes at 9.5–10 ka might point to a major earthquake as a common source event. At ca. 7 ka, the site fell dry and was covered by colluvial deposits. Our findings complement reconstructions of the regional glacial and postglacial evolution; however, the causes of lake‐level drops require further research.</jats:p>
authors: Lukas Gegg, Alexander Fülling, Andrew Greenwood, György Hetényi, F. Martin Hofmann, Giovanni Monegato, Jahir S. Rangel Herrera, Camille Schirra, Marco Venier, Othmar Müntener

<jats:title>ABSTRACT</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Extensive Salpausselkä ice‐marginal formations were deposited in southern and eastern Finland during the Weichselian deglaciation. These comprise three major ridges (I, II, and III Salpausselkäs) and their eastern counterparts (Tuupovaara, Koitere, and Pielisjärvi), together forming laterally continuous ice‐marginal formations extending approximately 650 km, with a total mapped length of 1530 km. Among the largest ice‐marginal deposits globally, the Salpausselkäs consist mainly of glaciofluvial sand and gravel, locally interbedded with till. They include ice‐contact deltas, subaqueous fans, sandurs, moraine slabs and ridges, and shoreline deposits, with depositional architecture strongly controlled by ice‐lobe dynamics, meltwater discharge, proglacial water depth, and bedrock topography. In this review, we synthesize the current understanding of the chronology, composition, and depositional environments of the Salpausselkäs, drawing together a substantial body of literature accumulated over the decades, including numerous studies published only in the Finnish language. Uncertainties related to their deposition, as well as topics requiring further investigation, are also discussed.</jats:p>

<jats:title>ABSTRACT</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>We present the results of geophysical surveys and LiDAR analysis of the Vallum and wider landscape at Milking Gap, on Hadrian's Wall. Magnetic gradiometry and Electrical Resistivity Tomography (ERT) surveys were utilised to investigate the landscape context of the Vallum and provide insight into the stratigraphy of the preserved earthworks. While the gradiometry data were affected by the geological background, surveys imaged discrete features with large magnetic gradient anomalies. We interpret these as simple lime‐kilns, potentially associated with pre‐Roman or Roman land‐use, or accumulations of dolerite derived from the nearby Whin Sill. ERT surveys imaged the stratigraphy of the Vallum mounds, although the ditch remained poorly constrained due to waterlogging. Resistivity contrasts within the mounds may be evidence of stony or compacted foundation layers. Interpretations are supported by known Roman strategies for the construction of turf monuments and site‐based observations. Separately, LiDAR hydrological analyses and modelling broaden our understanding of the monument's interaction with local hydrogeology. Importantly, we suggest that the north and the south mounds of the Vallum at the site may have been provisioned with primary gaps. If correct, these would be the only known examples of primary gaps apart from at forts and milecastles along the Wall.</jats:p>

<jats:p>
                    The French Mediterranean region, like others in southern Europe, is thought to have hosted glacial refugia for temperate plants and animals. At its heart, the Rhône valley appears to have been a pathway for various organisms towards the northern areas. Two well‐dated postglacial molluscan successions were investigated. They allow for the reconstruction of postglacial palaeoenvironments and recolonization stages by temperate snails. Particularly responsive to habitat structure, the mollusc fauna invites reassessment of the extent of Lateglacial and Early Holocene steppe‐like formations which often appear underestimated. Only a few species with forest affinities appear since
                    <jats:italic>c</jats:italic>
                    . 10 500 cal. a BP. They are not very demanding in terms of tree cover and their abundance remains insignificant. For taphonomic reasons, the only truly forest snails are found here late, as relicts of a maximum known elsewhere between
                    <jats:italic>c</jats:italic>
                    . 8000 and 7400 cal. a BP. After the Lateglacial, steppe and wooded steppe snail communities are exclusive throughout the Early Holocene. They correspond with the juniper shrub‐steppe of anthracologists between
                    <jats:italic>c</jats:italic>
                    . 11 400 and 8900 cal. a BP. The cold‐stage species
                    <jats:italic>Xerocrassa geyeri</jats:italic>
                    coexists until
                    <jats:italic>c</jats:italic>
                    . 10 400 cal. a BP with newly recruited xerothermic snails. The return of the endemic
                    <jats:italic>Candidula rugosiuscula</jats:italic>
                    , as early as 13 100 cal. a BP, suggests the existence of local refugia during the LGM and the preceding glacial stages.
                    <jats:italic>Backeljaia gigaxii</jats:italic>
                    , absent from the Pleistocene before the Late Glacial Interstadial (LGI), could be an immigrant. The existence of local glacial refugia for open‐ground Mediterranean snails remains a priority question. The role of local refugia for forest snails only becomes effective after the 9.3 ka event due to aridity. That of classical forest macrorefugia is not apparent. In the future, we will be able to refer to these stratigraphic sequences and their malacological content to correlate the scattered and incomplete successions that are most frequent in the Lateglacial and Early Holocene regional record.
                  </jats:p>

items.abstract: <jats:p>The Palaeolithic site of Ochtmissen (Lower Saxony, Germany) was excavated in fluvial terrace deposits during the winter of 1993/1994. The current study presents, for the first time, a thorough analysis of the lithic assemblage, encompassing its primary technological and typological characteristics, as well as the type and age of the fluvial deposits, in which the artefacts are embedded. Utilising an integrated approach encompassing all available data, we herein propose an attribution of the site to the (early?) MIS 4, thereby contributing a significant element to the ongoing discourse concerning the presence of humans north of 50° latitude during glacial periods in northern central Europe. Taking into account the information derived from the analysis of the technical and typological composition of the lithic assemblage, the stratigraphic and sedimentological data available from the excavation records, we propose an interpretation of the site's occupation strategy as sporadic yet recurring, and possibly seasonal. Taken together, all these data make a substantial contribution with new insights into the ongoing extensive debate regarding the modalities, extent and patterns of interaction between Neanderthal groups, the landscape and the climate in Europe.</jats:p>

<jats:title>ABSTRACT</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    Sexual dimorphism in the human infracranial skeleton has been extensively studied, yet its structural organization across skeletal regions remains incompletely characterized at a global scale. Using a geographically diverse sample of 3177 individuals of known sex (1219 females; 1958 males) drawn from five documented skeletal collections, this study quantifies sexual dimorphism across 12 long bones measurements of the humerus, radius, femur, and tibia. Dimorphism indices (DS%), two‐way ANOVAs with partial
                    <jats:italic>η</jats:italic>
                    <jats:sup>2</jats:sup>
                    , Mahalanobis distances, Hedges'
                    <jats:italic>g</jats:italic>
                    , and
                    <jats:italic>D</jats:italic>
                    ‐index were computed to characterize the magnitude and the consistency of sex differences across groups. Results reveal a clear anatomical gradient in the expression of sexual dimorphism. Maximum bone lengths exhibit the lowest dimorphism (DS% = 8.5%–11.5%) with high stability and low within‐sex variability. Articular breadths show the strongest association with sex (partial
                    <jats:italic>η</jats:italic>
                    <jats:sup>2</jats:sup>
                    > 56%) combined with relatively low intra‐sexual dispersion. Diaphyseal diameters, particularly in the upper limb, display the highest DS% values but also the greatest coefficients of variation, reflecting greater biomechanical and methodological sensitivity. Sex × Group interactions are weak or non‐significant across all variables, and rank concordance analyses confirm that this hierarchical pattern is consistent across populations (Kendall's
                    <jats:italic>W</jats:italic>
                     = 0.707–0.814,
                    <jats:italic>p</jats:italic>
                     < 0.001). These findings strongly support previous studies demonstrating the reliability of articular breadths for sex estimation in skeletal remains, and confirm that the metric signal of sexual dimorphism in long bones reflects a fundamental and broadly shared structural organization of the human appendicular skeleton.
                  </jats:p>

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    The oropharyngeal cavity of turtles exhibits considerable morphological diversity associated with differences in habitat, diet, and feeding strategies. However, the structural organization of this region remains poorly characterized in many Testudines, including
                    <jats:italic>Kinosternon scorpioides scorpioides</jats:italic>
                    , therefore, we aim to characterize the morphological aspects of the oropharyngeal cavity of
                    <jats:italic>K. s. scorpioides</jats:italic>
                    reported using macroscopic descriptions, light microscopy (LM) and scanning electron microscopy (SEM). LM revealed that almost the entire epithelium lining the oropharyngeal cavity of
                    <jats:italic>K. s. scorpioides</jats:italic>
                    is of the non‐keratinized stratified mucous type, containing many mucous cells and numerous mucous glands throughout the lingual epithelium, palate and floor of the mouth, with the exception of the region located near the rhinopharynx, which presented a stratified keratinized squamous epithelial tissue containing taste buds, not observed on the tongue. SEM revealed that the entire epithelium of the oropharyngeal cavity has pores that are likely associated with the mucous glands observed in LM, and the surface of the tongue is covered by voluminous lingual papillae of varying sizes and shapes (filiform and fungiform types), which had cells covered by microvilli and/or microcysts. No salivary glands were observed. Compared with morphological data from other species, this study indicates that the epithelial structure of the oropharyngeal cavity of
                    <jats:italic>K. s. scorpioides</jats:italic>
                    is consistent with that observed in other generalist omnivores with semi‐aquatic habits, thus corresponding to ecological information about this species.
                  </jats:p>

<jats:title>ABSTRACT</jats:title>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Objectives</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Comparing children's growth across the world and at different moments in history can yield insight into both health challenges and healthy morphological variation in humans. A difficulty of such comparative analyses is that, in marginalized populations, there are often logistical complications to obtaining repeat measures of individual children's height and weight. The problem is even more acute for historical populations: bioarcheological datasets comprise single measures of individuals at death. Additionally, for both contemporary and historical populations, there is often non‐trivial uncertainty about children's ages. Both of these factors complicate estimation of growth trajectories. Here we evaluate the degree to which we can accurately estimate a population‐mean growth trajectory using only a small number of (randomly) uncertain measurements, like those that compose many contemporary and bioarcheological datasets.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Materials and Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>We recently derived a causal model of human growth from fundamental principles of metabolism and allometry, permitting exploration of genetic and environmental contributions to children's growth. Here, we fit this model in a Bayesian framework to simulated cross‐sectional and longitudinal datasets of varying size, where age is uncertain.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>For large‐scale comparisons, reasonably accurate population‐mean growth trajectories may be obtained from single height measures of 100 children of a given sex and a range of ages. However, detailed analyses of pubertal growth spurts and the metabolic and allometric parameters underlying growth require longitudinal datasets.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Discussion</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>We conclude that this new model and estimation strategy constitute a potentially useful toolkit for comparing mean growth trajectories across contemporary and historical populations.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

items.title: Estimating Mean Growth Trajectories When Measurements Are Sparse and Age Is Uncertain

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    The inner ear of vertebrates serves dual roles, detecting sound as well as maintaining equilibrium. The increased accessibility of Computed Tomography (CT) provides an opportunity to assess the morphology of the skeletal labyrinth, which houses the membranous labyrinth of the ear, in one of the two primary clades of elasmobranchs: Squalomorphi. This study describes the morphology of the skeletal labyrinth of 10 species of squalomorphs:
                    <jats:italic>Chlamydoselachus anguineus</jats:italic>
                    ,
                    <jats:italic>Heptranchias perlo, Hexanchus griseus</jats:italic>
                    ,
                    <jats:italic>Notorynchus cepedianus, Squatina californica</jats:italic>
                    ,
                    <jats:italic>Centrophorus squamosus, Squaliolus laticaudus, Oxynotus centrina, Isistius brasiliensis</jats:italic>
                    , and
                    <jats:italic>Etmopterus bullisi</jats:italic>
                    . Hexanchiformes are found to have more robust skeletal labyrinth spaces housing the semicircular canals and ampullae, while taxa from Order Squaliformes have more slender labyrinths. Given the variety in diet and habitat across this sample of taxa, we advocate for broader taxonomic coverage and finer assessment of ecological categories in the future, as well as quantitative assessments of ear geometry and its relationship with phylogenetic history, locomotion, and habitat.
                  </jats:p>
items.summary: 《现存角鲨目鲨类骨骼迷路的比较形态学》：该研究利用CT描述了10种角鲨目鲨类内耳骨骼迷路的形态，发现六鳃鲨目容纳半规管和壶腹的迷路空间更为粗壮，而角鲨目类群迷路更细长，并建议未来扩大分类覆盖并量化耳部几何形态与系统发育、运动和栖息地的关系，适合关注软骨鱼类感觉器官演化与形态适应者阅读。
items.title: Comparative morphology of the skeletal labyrinth in extant squalomorph sharks

                  <jats:p>

items.summary: 《内蒙古乌兰塔塔尔戈壁荒漠兔新材料为鼠兔科起源提供形态学证据》：研究报道了在内蒙古乌兰塔塔尔早渐新世地层中首次发现的戈壁荒漠兔头骨及保存完好的上颌骨和下颌骨，通过形态对比与系统发育分析支持鼠兔科的单系性，并将荒漠兔置于该科最基部位置，确认其为鼠兔科最早成员，同时探讨了鼠兔科形态特征的演化阶段及幼年标本中特殊的乳齿替换顺序。

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    The Chinese alligator (
                    <jats:italic>Alligator sinensis</jats:italic>
                    ) is a small crocodilian endemic to China; current neuroanatomical knowledge of its whole brain remains limited. In the present study, we combined the Micro‐Optical Sectioning Tomography system with Imaris, CorelDRAW, and MATLAB software to generate a histological atlas of the entire Chinese alligator brain and reconstruct its 3D digital brain model. Results showed that the whole brain of the Chinese alligator is anatomically partitioned into eight major compartments: olfactory bulb (OB), olfactory tract (OTr), telencephalon (Tel), diencephalon (Dien), mesencephalon (Mes), cerebellum (Cer), pituitary gland (PG), and medulla oblongata (MO). Most distinguishable cytoarchitectonic structures reside within the Tel, Dien, and Mes. The main OB exhibits a finely laminated cytoarchitecture, whereas an accessory olfactory bulb (AOB) is absent. Collectively, the Tel and Dien occupy approximately one‐third of the total brain volume. The mesencephalic tectum displays distinct laminar organization, with the corpora quadrigemina (CQ) differentiated into superior and inferior colliculi. A total of 116 discrete brain structures were annotated in this atlas. We unambiguously identified a pineal body (PB) in the Chinese alligator, substantially expanding the fundamental neurohistological dataset of crocodilian brains. This work establishes a foundational morphological template for reptilian nervous system research and provides critical comparative anatomical references for evolutionary neurobiology across all vertebrate lineages.
                  </jats:p>
items.summary: 《中华鳖全脑二维结构标注与三维重建》：研究结合显微光学切片断层成像与多种软件，构建了中华鳖全脑组织学图谱和三维数字模型，将全脑划分为嗅球、嗅束、端脑、间脑、中脑、小脑、垂体和延髓八大区域，标注116个离散脑结构，并明确鉴定出松果体。该工作扩充了鳄类脑神经组织学基础数据，为爬行动物神经系统研究和脊椎动物演化神经生物学比较解剖提供了参考。

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    Amphisbaenians (Squamata: Amphisbaenidae) are fossorial reptiles with highly specialized cranial morphology, yet their fossil record is frequently limited by fragmentary preservation. This study provides a detailed osteological redescription of the skulls of
                    <jats:italic>Amphisbaena braestrupi</jats:italic>
                    and
                    <jats:italic>Amphisbaena laurenti</jats:italic>
                    from the Pleistocene of Lagoa Santa (Brazil) using high‐resolution x‐ray computed tomography. Beyond surface morphology, 3D reconstructions allowed the first detailed visualization of previously inaccessible internal anatomical features, such as the complex architecture of the braincase and the parabasal and optic canals. The analysis revealed hourglass‐shaped skulls with pronounced sagittal crests and an advanced degree of coossification in the occipital complex. Digital dissection enabled the description of the pyramidal morphology of the otic capsules and the arrangement of the semicircular canals, alongside a more comprehensive redescription of the fossil material. Comparisons with the extant species
                    <jats:italic>Amphisbaena alba</jats:italic>
                    show that the fossils reach the upper limit of cranial size variation and exhibit greater occipital robustness. These findings fill critical anatomical gaps, providing new internal characters for taxonomic, phylogenetic, and evolutionary studies of South American amphisbaenians.
                  </jats:p>

items.title: Redescription of the cranial morphology of Amphisbaena braestrupi and Amphisbaena laurenti (Squamata: Amphisbaenidae) from the Pleistocene of Brazil using x‐ray computed tomography

<jats:title>ABSTRACT</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    Anthropogenic carbonate deposits in Roman aqueducts can provide detailed environmental and archaeological information. The Roman aqueduct of Nîmes (France), famed for the Pont du Gard bridge, was built around
                    <jats:sc>AD</jats:sc>
                    50 to convey water over 50 km to the city of
                    <jats:italic>Nemausus</jats:italic>
                    for drinking and bathing. Anthropogenic carbonate deposited along its channel was investigated using a multi‐proxy approach combining stable C, O and Sr isotopes with trace elements to understand ancient water management strategies and environmental conditions. δ
                    <jats:sup>13</jats:sup>
                    C values and Sr isotopes show that another water source was added to the system after 11 years of operation, coinciding with a dry spell. After 100 years, water delivery to the city decreased, probably due to water abstraction for irrigation in the countryside. After another 120 years, the city water supply ceased entirely, coinciding with an empire‐wide economic crisis and the Plague of Cyprian (
                    <jats:sc>AD</jats:sc>
                    250–270). The upstream part of the aqueduct, however, including the Pont du Gard, remained operational for at least another 140 years, primarily for irrigation. The carbonate deposits record hydroclimate dynamics and human interference over 220–360 years during the Roman period, and dating the breakdown of parts of the system provides insights into urban change.
                  </jats:p>
items.summary: 《尼姆渡槽使用史：基于碳酸盐档案的重建——运行、改造与晚古期崩溃及变迁》：研究利用稳定碳、氧、锶同位素与微量元素多指标分析渡槽中的碳酸盐沉积，重建罗马尼姆渡槽约220至360年间的运行与改造过程，揭示新增水源、灌溉分流及城市供水终止与帝国经济危机和瘟疫的关联，并发现上游包括加尔桥段仍延续运行至少140年，为理解古代水资源管理与城市变迁提供具体证据。
items.title: The Usage History of the Aqueduct of Nîmes Reconstructed From Carbonate Archives: Operation, Modifications and Late Antique Breakdown and Change

items.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>The inner ear is among the most intricate and complex structures in the body. Housed deep within the petrous temporal bone, it contains the organs for audition and balance. Our understanding of its structure and function has relied heavily on advances in imaging and novel visualization modalities. This review synthesizes the historical and technological progression of research on inner ear structure, tracing developments from early philosophical speculation and gross dissection to microscopy, serial histology, radiographic imaging, and contemporary high‐resolution digital modalities. We outline three major eras in inner ear investigation: the classical period, during which the ear was considered solely an auditory organ; the Renaissance and early modern period, marked by transformative anatomical illustration and the recognition of labyrinthine structure; and the modern era, characterized by experimental demonstration of vestibular function, high‐resolution in situ imaging, and the refinement of quantitative morphological analyses. Several recent innovations, including micro‐computed tomography, contrast‐enhanced imaging, super‐resolution microscopy, high‐field magnetic resonance imaging, and advanced three‐dimensional segmentation techniques, have substantially improved spatial resolution and soft‐tissue visualization. As a result, these developments have enabled increasingly precise reconstruction of both osseous and membranous labyrinthine structures. These approaches are shifting the field from descriptive anatomy toward integrative, quantitative, and functionally informed models of inner ear biology. Furthermore, forays into in vivo imaging are pushing the bounds of anatomical imaging. This review situates contemporary advances within their historical context. In doing so, we highlight the most impactful contributions to our understanding of inner ear structure, evolution, and disease—and identify questions that remain unresolved. Continued refinement of in vivo and post‐mortem in situ visualization modalities promises to bridge anatomical detail with physiological function and clinical phenotype, advancing basic science and translational otology.</jats:p>

items.title: Visualizing the inner ear: Historical perspectives and future directions to elucidate labyrinth structure and function

items.abstract:
<jats:title>ABSTRACT</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Human reproduction presents features that appear inefficient in isolation: gamete overproduction, mechanically demanding birth, neonatal altriciality, lactational suppression of fertility, reproductive cessation, prolonged post‐reproductive survival, and extensive care by individuals other than parents. Evolutionary accounts increasingly explain such features through conflict among parties with divergent fitness interests. We argue that conflict loses discriminating power when the term is extended to physical limits, to cooperative interactions, and to trade‐offs within a single organism, and that this loss occurs as a formally derived concept becomes a framing metaphor in synthetic and applied literatures. We set out an explanatory architecture in which four processes—genetic conflict, constraint, cooperative dependence, and life‐history allocation—occupy distinct positions within a single optimization structure: constraint specifies the feasible set and the shape of the benefit and cost functions, allocation identifies the optimum for one party within it, and conflict and cooperative dependence describe how many parties hold optima on the same joint phenotype and whether their marginal interests oppose or align. A cross‐cutting temporal dimension covers traits whose consequences fall on one individual at more than one time. We restate conflict as a claim about marginal rather than total fitness returns, so that shared benefit neither establishes nor refutes it. Explicit coding rules assign nine phenomena a primary architecture and contributing processes, with evidence status, standing in the literature, and discriminating predictions. Two worked cases—the obstetrical dilemma and lactational amenorrhea—convert contested labels into separable empirical programs. The framework does not settle these questions; it specifies which measurements would.</jats:p>
items.summary: 《冲突、约束、合作与分配：人类生殖悖论的多元演化架构》：该文主张将“冲突”概念限定于边际适应度回报，提出由遗传冲突、约束、合作依赖与生活史分配四过程构成的统一优化架构，并据此为九种生殖现象编码，还以产科困境与哺乳期闭经两个案例说明如何把争议标签转化为可分离的实证研究方案，适合关注人类生殖演化解释框架的读者。
items.title: Conflict, Constraint, Cooperation, and Allocation: A Plural Evolutionary Architecture for Human Reproductive Paradoxes

items.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Worldwide, lacustrine ecosystems are threatened by eutrophication and deoxygenation. Both processes are driven by the combined effects of human activities and climate change. Understanding the pre‐anthropogenic nexus between warming, eutrophication, deoxygenation, and related feedback is essential to determine how lakes respond to rapid climate change. We investigate the responses of primary producers, stratification, and nutrient cycling in a small Central European lake (Übeschisee, Swiss Plateau) to rapid climate change during Late Glacial times (17–11 ka). After 16.2 ka (Heinrich Stadial; HS1) and during the Bølling/Allerød interstadial, Übeschisee experienced natural eutrophication following summer warming and vegetation development in the catchment. Anoxia events with blooms of sulfur bacteria systematically established during colder periods of HS1 (16.5 ka), the Older Dryas (14 ka), the Gerzensee Oscillation (13.2 ka), and the Younger Dryas (12.7–11.7 ka). Anoxia events also caused reductive dissolution of Mn; labile P was always efficiently recycled. Algal communities responded to anoxia events, but the excursions of community composition were reversible. Ti follows NGRIP Dust, suggesting that Übeschisee provides a continuous record of dust deposition with high rates during colder periods. The paired lake approach with adjacent Amsoldingersee shows that the results are robust and regionally reproducible, and that common drivers influenced both lakes simultaneously.</jats:p>
items.summary: 《晚冰期气候变化的初级生产者、缺氧与化学反馈：基于配对湖泊研究的启示》：研究通过瑞士高原于贝希湖与相邻湖泊的配对分析，探讨晚冰期快速气候变化下湖泊初级生产者、分层与营养循环的响应，发现变暖后出现自然富营养化，寒冷期反复出现缺氧与硫细菌繁盛，且藻类群落变化可逆，值得关注其对湖泊脱氧与富营养化机制的启示。
items.title: Responses of primary producers, anoxia, and chemical feedback to Late Glacial climate change: Insights from a paired lake approach

items.abstract:
<jats:title>ABSTRACT</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    The Cadí Massif (42°17′09″ N, 1°38′11″ E; 2649 m a.s.l.) in the southeastern Pyrenees preserves clear evidence of Late Pleistocene glaciation, although previous research has focused almost exclusively on its northern slope. By contrast, the southern slope has remained largely unexplored. In this study, we present the first glacial geochronology for this sector by combining
                    <jats:sup>36</jats:sup>
                    Cl terrestrial cosmogenic nuclide (TCN) surface‐exposure dating with numerical paleoclimate modeling. We analyzed 18 boulder samples collected from moraines in two major cirques to constrain the timing of glacier fluctuations. Although some exposure ages were interpreted as reflecting post‐depositional disturbance or possible nuclide inheritance, the resulting chronology indicates that the upper plateaus and southern cirques remained glaciated during the late stages of deglaciation following the Last Glacial Cycle, while subsequent moraine systems document later glacial advances. These include small snowdrift glaciers, up to
                    <jats:italic>ca</jats:italic>
                    . 4 km in length, that persisted during the Younger Dryas stadial at
                    <jats:italic>ca</jats:italic>
                    . 12–13 ka, with their mass balance sustained largely by wind‐driven snow redistribution and avalanche‐fed accumulation. Paleoclimate simulations indicate that temperatures were
                    <jats:italic>ca</jats:italic>
                    . 3°C lower during that phase, while precipitation was comparable to present‐day conditions. This integrated approach demonstrates the sensitivity of southern‐slope glaciers to abrupt climate shifts and provides a more comprehensive view of the spatial variability of glacial responses across the Cadí Massif and the broader Eastern Pyrenees.
                  </jats:p>
items.summary: 《东南比利牛斯山脉卡迪地块南部晚更新世冰川作用的新年代学约束》：研究首次为卡迪地块南坡建立冰川年代学，结合36Cl宇宙成因核素暴露测年与古气候模拟，分析两个冰斗的18个漂砾样品，揭示晚冰期冰川波动及约12至13 ka新仙女木期由风驱雪再分配和雪崩补给维持的小型冰川，并模拟当时降温约3°C。适合关注比利牛斯山冰川响应与古气候重建的读者。
items.title: New geochronological constraints on Late Pleistocene glaciation in the southern Cadí Massif, SE Pyrenees

items.abstract:
<jats:title>ABSTRACT</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    Changes in fire activity are recognized as a major threat to biodiversity and vegetation communities across the Mediterranean Basin. However, long‐term fire–vegetation interactions remain poorly investigated. Here, we combine a high‐resolution charcoal record with pollen data from the “
                    <jats:italic>Étang des Aulnes</jats:italic>
                    ” lake (southern France) to reconstruct the last ~8000 years of fire dynamics and assess its influence on vegetation communities and diversity. A significant result is that the highest level of fire frequency and burned biomass occurred around 4200 cal a
                    <jats:sc>BP</jats:sc>
                    , coinciding with the decline of deciduous oak forests and their replacement by evergreen oak forests/scrublands. Moreover, the relationship between taxonomic richness and burned biomass is assessed and shows that taxonomic richness reaches its maximum at intermediate burned biomass levels. We discuss here how fire may explain this relationship, as well as its limitations, which are influenced by variations in environmental and land‐use conditions. Together, these findings illustrate how long‐term fire dynamics influence vegetation diversity and community trajectories and highlight the structuring role of interacting drivers, such as fire, herbivory, and anthropogenic activities, in Mediterranean ecosystems.
                  </jats:p>
items.summary: 《全新世法国地中海地区的植被变化与火-植物多样性变迁》：该研究结合法国南部湖泊的高分辨率炭屑记录与孢粉数据，重建了过去约8000年的火动态，发现火频率与燃烧生物量在约4200年前达到峰值，与落叶栎林衰退及常绿栎林/灌丛取而代之同步，并评估了分类丰富度与燃烧生物量的关系，显示丰富度在中等燃烧生物量水平达到最大。
items.title: Holocene vegetation change and fire–plant diversity shifts in Mediterranean France

items.abstract:
<jats:title>ABSTRACT</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Studies on biomobility in the Indus Valley Civilisation (IVC) or the Harappan Culture provide important insights into pastoral practices, trade and environmental adaptation that shaped the civilisation's economy and social networks. At its height, the IVC engaged in extensive trade across its vast territory, resulting in cultural and economic change across diverse ecological zones. Although archaeological finds indicate trade in artefacts throughout the civilisation, our understanding of human and animal mobility remains limited due to a lack of geochemical and isotopic data on provenance. A key unresolved issue in biomobility is distinguishing between local and broader animal husbandry practices and their trade connections. To address this, we analysed faunal teeth, bone bioapatite and bone‐encased soil using C–O–Sr–Nd isotopes from two Harappan sites, Kanmer (Gujarat) and Tigrana (Haryana), located more than 900 km apart. Our isotope data and the existing literature suggest that, in Kanmer, specialised animal‐feeding methods were used, and local rainfall was the primary water source across all settlements. Data from both sites show that most sheep/goat were raised locally with little movement; however, bovines in Kanmer from the mature and late‐mature phases had diverse, possibly non‐local origins, likely from Haryana. At Tigrana, some animals also showed signs of movement from nearby regions. Regional movement of bovines from a better watered region to a semi‐arid region may indicate trading as an important aspect of this civilisation embedded within broader social and economic networks.</jats:p>

<jats:p>
                    The Dinaric Mountains are a mountain range stretching NW–SE from the Alps to the Albanides–Hellenides in central Europe. The highest parts were occupied by small ice fields and/or valley glaciers during the Quaternary cold periods, while even today some small glaciers still exist in topoclimatically favourable areas. The northernmost part of the Dinaric Mountains is called Trnovski Gozd (1495 m a.s.l.). It is a high karst plateau characterized by conical hills, uvalas, solution dolines, and numerous speleological features. In addition to the karst, Trnovski Gozd also has a palaeoglacial landscape above 1100 m a.s.l. Here, we present the glacial history of Trnovski Gozd, which was studied using geomorphological mapping, terrestrial cosmogenic nuclide (TCN,
                    <jats:sup>36</jats:sup>
                    Cl) dating, and the Parallel Ice Sheet Modelling (PISM). The glacial evidence on the Trnovski Gozd is very scattered and sparse. Geomorphological mapping suggests a glaciated area of ~6 km
                    <jats:sup>2</jats:sup>
                    . Five samples from boulders located on the crest of the largest moraine in the area were dated. The results yield a median age of 19.5±2.1 ka (corrected for a denudation rate of 20 mm ka
                    <jats:sup>−1</jats:sup>
                    ) and are consistent with ages of the global Last Glacial Maximum (LGM). None of the Parallel Ice Sheet Model (PISM) simulations fully reproduce the geomorphologically reconstructed glacier extent. However, a scenario employing a temperature offset of −7.0 °C and a precipitation scaling factor of 0.95 relative to modern values provide the best fit, yielding a glaciated area of 27.4 km
                    <jats:sup>2</jats:sup>
                    while successfully reproducing the position of the dated moraine. The Equilibrium Line Altitude (ELA) derived from the simulation results equals 1246 m a.s.l. and is similar to the LGM ELAs of some nearby isolated alpine glaciers. The temperature and precipitation offsets are also consistent with those observed across the Alps during the LGM. Reconstructions of isolated glaciers near the Alpine ice stream network provide valuable benchmarks for evaluating and refining palaeoclimate models.
                  </jats:p>

items.abstract: <jats:p>The AlpIce‐1 database is the first compilation of published geomorphological and geochronological markers constraining build‐up, culmination and decay of glaciers from the Last Glacial Maximum through the Holocene across the entire European Alps. AlpIce‐1 integrates more than 4200 surface‐exposure and radiocarbon ages, homogenized, quality controlled and evaluated for their palaeoglaciological context, compiled from 268 peer‐reviewed publications and over 1300 sites across the European Alps. The database includes ages originally obtained from a wide range of landforms and deposits including moraine ridges, lakes, mires, sediment outcrops, ice cores, bedrock surfaces, caves and archaeological sites. It documents chronological constraints on more than 1400 palaeoglacial events, including past ice‐margin stabilization, ice (re‐)advance, ice retreat, ice‐free or ice‐cover conditions. A GIS catalogue of more than 260 dated landforms (e.g. moraines, rock glaciers, landslide deposits) complements the database. AlpIce‐1 is designed as an open‐access resource supporting both field and modelling studies across the Alps and is intended for all communities interested in the late Quaternary. In light of emerging next‐generation numerical ice models, AlpIce‐1 offers an extensive and robust empirical basis for evaluating future (palaeo)glacier simulations.</jats:p>

items.abstract: <jats:p>The glacierized Valle Frías in Northern Patagonia is one of the best‐studied valleys in South America and includes varved sediments from Lago Frías. We complement this lacustrine record with a high‐resolution documentation of varve counts and their composition. Geochemical and grain size analyses support their interpretation as proglacial varves attributed to over‐ and interflows resulting from snow‐ and glacier melt. Integration of radiometric, tephra and historic ages with microfacies analyses and semi‐automatic varve counting utilizing high‐resolution images obtained by computed tomography provides a calendar‐year chronology consisting of an upper (1960–2019 CE) and a floating lower varve chronology (1803–1893 CE). Intercalated between both varved sections are two event layers: a tephra resulting from the eruption of Volcán Calbuco (1893 CE) directly followed by an erosive mass‐wasting deposit associated with the Great Chilean Earthquake (1960 CE). Statistical comparison of varve‐thickness measurements with instrumental temperature data and dendroclimatological summer‐temperature reconstruction on an annual basis indicates only a weak temperature control on varve thickness. However, analysis of decadal means documents that the occurrence of thicker varves in the 21st century coincides with warmer summers.</jats:p>

<jats:title>ABSTRACT</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    In this paper, we present a systematic method focused on petrographic analysis to identify different steps in the pottery production process and use this method to evaluate Rio Grande Glaze Ware from the Rio Abajo region of New Mexico. Working within the framework of
                    <jats:italic>chaîne opératoire</jats:italic>
                    , we examine the pottery production sequence by measuring ceramic attributes that reflect choices made at different steps in the process. We argue that our method can detect changes in the production sequence over time, but not all changes occurred simultaneously or for the same reason. Also, not all changes affected the final appearance of the vessels, making petrography a critical tool for detecting change in less visible attributes. Ultimately, we argue that our method can be used across space and time to explore various questions of technological practice. While our case study is focused on Ancestral Pueblo culture, this kind of research is obviously not exclusive to the southwest United States but can be examined in pottery‐producing cultures across the globe. Methods that use petrographic analysis for studies beyond the determination of provenance are a valuable contribution to the field of archeology.
                  </jats:p>

<jats:title>ABSTRACT</jats:title>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Objectives</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Platycnemia, a mediolateral flattening of the tibial shaft, has been argued to be an adult phenomenon caused by mechanical forces shaping bone. Here we investigate the possibility that this condition develops prior to growth plate closure, at a time when the epiphyseal cartilage is responsive to torsional loading.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Materials and Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>We analyze the degree of torsion along the tibial shaft and compare that to the cnemic index (a measure of platycnemia) in two populations: ancient Jomon and modern Japanese. Through linear mixed‐effects modeling, we aimed to determine whether platycnemia, as measured by the cnemic index, is correlated with the magnitude of torsion that the tibia undergoes during development, prior to growth plate closure.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Our results show that cnemic index significantly decreases as individuals age and the tibia lengthens, resulting in increasing mediolateral flattening and greater instances of platycnemia. However, we found no significant relationship between tibial torsion and the cnemic index.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Discussion</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Our findings suggest that a broader range of genetic, biomechanical, and environmental properties needs to be considered when hypothesizing how skeletal modeling might be related to the development of platycnemia.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

<jats:title>ABSTRACT</jats:title>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Objectives</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>In many rural regions of developing countries, increasing market access is reshaping local food systems. Traditional diets rooted in local agriculture are being replaced by market‐driven alternatives. It is suspected that this dietary transition will contribute to rising risks of non‐communicable diseases through increased chronic inflammation. This study, conducted in northern Lao People's Democratic Republic, investigated the association between dietary transition and concentrations of C‐reactive protein (CRP) as a biomarker of chronic inflammation in three villages with varying levels of market exposure.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Data were collected from 380 adults in three villages with different degrees of market integration. Questionnaires recorded individual characteristics and weekly intake frequency of 28 food groups. Dried blood spots were analyzed for CRP using enzyme‐linked immunosorbent assay. Dietary patterns were identified using principal component analysis, and scores were compared among villages. Associations between dietary patterns and CRP were examined using multivariable logistic regression. To account for seasonality, analyses were conducted within same‐season subgroups: rainy (Na Lae, Na Savang) and dry (Na Savang, Nam Nyon).</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>CRP concentrations were higher in villages with a higher degree of market integration. A dietary pattern was identified, characterized by high consumption of foraged wild plants and a low intake of market‐related foods. This pattern was negatively associated with elevated CRP in the dry season subsample.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusions</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Higher CRP concentrations were found in residents of villages with a higher degree of market integration. This trend may partly be explained by a dietary transition from a foraging‐based to a market‐dependent diet.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

items.abstract: <jats:p>Coastal erosion of glacigenic sediments, particularly in the form of retreating drumlin bluffs, is a key process in paraglacial landscape evolution during periods of relative sea‐level (RSL) rise. As marine transgression reworks formerly subaerial glacial terrains, drumlins act as discrete sediment sources generating characteristic erosional and depositional drowned landforms. In this study, we identify extensive fields of submerged truncated sediment drumlins across several locations in the Irish Sea and along the western Scottish seaboard. The drumlins were formed during maximum and retreat phases of the last British‐Irish Ice Sheet (BIIS). They now exhibit flat‐topped morphologies often associated with gravel tails, tombolos and coalesced platforms, closely resembling previously described examples of eroding drumlin coasts from the west coast of Ireland and North America. The geomorphic assemblages are consistent with wave‐driven erosion of drumlin bluffs during lower sea‐level stands, and we interpret the truncated drumlins as terrestrial‐limiting indicators of past RSL. Comparison with existing RSL reconstructions and glacio‐isostatic adjustment (GIA) models reveals discrepancies between observed truncation depths and predicted sea‐level minima, suggesting that current models may underestimate lowstand magnitudes in parts of Britain and Ireland. These findings highlight the potential of submarine geomorphological records to refine regional sea‐level reconstructions and improve understanding of post‐glacial coastal evolution.</jats:p>

items.title: Truncated drumlins and their implication for past sea level reconstructions

items.abstract: <jats:p>Tephra layers may be studied to understand the dynamics and sequence of past explosive volcanism. In Iceland, the distinctive Settlement Layer (AD ~877) underlies almost all archaeological evidence for the Norse Settlement and is preserved in soils across Iceland and as cryptotephra overseas. It comprises an olive‐green, tholeiitic basalt unit erupted from the Vatnaöldur crater row (within the Veiðivötn fissure swarm) and a white transitional alkali rhyolite unit from the Hrafntinnuhraun craters (within the Torfajökull complex). This paper describes a previously undocumented, dark‐grey tephra unit that we discovered in the Búland landholding (Skaftárhreppur). Electron probe micro‐analyses determined that this tephra unit is a bimodal transitional alkali basalt. Although it was deposited less than a year before the Vatnaöldur unit, it is unclear whether it also preceded the Hrafntinnuhraun unit. Nonetheless, we use the unit's thickness and composition to infer the likely origin to be Skyggnishlíðarvötn, a triplet of maar craters SW of the Torfajökull complex. The major‐/minor‐oxide composition of tephra collected from within the crater rim of the Skyggnishlíðarvötn maars (~45 km WNW of Búland) is indistinguishable from that of the unit we recorded near Búland. These findings demonstrate that volcanic unrest in the Veiðivötn fissure swarm is associated with explosive basaltic volcanism in the Torfajökull complex. The Skyggnishlíðarvötn phase may well have acted as a precursor to the impending Settlement eruption sequence.</jats:p>

<jats:title>ABSTRACT</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Irremovable silica and iron deposits, as well as dissolution etching on Paleoindian lithic artifacts from Grass Valley, Nevada, can imitate wear polish and obscure use‐wear traces on lithic tools. Previously unrecognized on Great Basin artifacts, researchers unfamiliar with such accumulations may mistake silica crusts on buried artifacts for carbonates or fail to recognize silica‐glazed or etched artifacts without examination under magnification. Because these deposits cannot be entirely removed without artifact damage, our goal is to describe their genesis and effects so other researchers can recognize and avoid misinterpreting them in future lithic studies. This study describes the alterations and processes that create these phenomena, places them in regional and specific contexts, identifies the types and sources of iron and silica involved, and examines variation with toolstone type, landform age and stability, soil type, pH, and depth below the surface. These processes are likely to affect lithic artifacts elsewhere in a broad region of arid North America west of the Cascade and Sierra Nevada mountains with tephra‐rich duric soils and in other regions with similar climate, sources of silica, and soil chemistry.</jats:p>

<jats:title>ABSTRACT</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>The Oshara Tradition is the classic culture‐historical framework used for the Archaic period in the American Southwest. It was defined during fieldwork conducted by Cynthia Irwin‐Williams for the Anasazi Origins Project (AOP) in the 1960s and early 1970s. Chapin has provided an overview of many of the excavated sites from the AOP, with the exception of the La Bajada site, which is the Type site for the Bajada phase, though it has never been reported on. We present the results of geologic, geomorphic, and bifacial technological studies of this site. A newly identified dacite/andesite source was used for manufacturing Bajada points at the La Bajada site. The surface of the site is relatively stable, with most of the artifacts being recovered from on or near surface contexts. The reduction trajectory for the points involved the use of large biface blanks from local materials. The Early Archaic foragers residing at the La Bajada site moved seasonally along a south‐north corridor across approximately 185 km.</jats:p>

<jats:title>ABSTRACT</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    Within archaeology there is a growing shift away from the purely aesthetic towards making the past relevant to present and future needs and demands. The
                    <jats:italic>Past Water Futures</jats:italic>
                    project charts the impact of ancient dam rehabilitation on climate change‐induced water scarcity in the North Central Andes. The rehabilitation of late period (AD 750–1532) Prehispanic dams is a novel approach to assuage increasing water shortage among the rural communities of the Andean highlands. Nevertheless, until now, we lacked data on the real‐time impact of these modern conservation and rehabilitation projects. Here we present preliminary results, including volume capacity, potential demand, hydrological and hydraulic analysis and a reservoir filling log of the Prehispanic Weetacocha ‘Lake of Flowers’ Dam, which was rehabilitated in late 2024. Weetacocha belongs to the rural community of Racratumanka, District of Pamparomás, Province of Huaylas, Ancash Region, Peru. Importantly, we analyse the cost per m
                    <jats:sup>3</jats:sup>
                    unit of water recovered through the rehabilitation of the Weetacocha Dam, proving that the restoration of water dams can provide a viable, cost‐effective, community‐led, sustainable alternative to modern micro‐dam construction in the Central Andes and potentially further afield.
                  </jats:p>

items.abstract: <jats:p>End moraines are formed at glacier ice margins and show the extent of former glaciations. Here in this review article, we use a fourfold genetic classification of end moraines (dump moraines, push moraines, lodge moraines and hummocky end moraines) to highlight the importance of lodge moraines, which are end moraines composed primarily of subglacial till deposited submarginally at and near the ice margin. Such end moraines were named ‘lodge moraines’ by Chamberlin (1894) in the same article that defined push moraines and dump moraines. We review the use of the term but emphasize that many end moraines are made in this manner without having received a genetic name. Lodge moraines are among the largest moraines in the world, some more than 10 km wide. They are especially common at the former margins of the lobes that drained the southern Laurentide Ice Sheet but have also been described in Iceland and Scandinavia. They are typically asymmetric with a steeper distal side. Because of their size, relatively few lodge moraines have received extensive sedimentological analysis, and an interpretation as a lodge moraine here is based largely on geomorphology and boreholes that reveal thick, uniform subglacial till similar to the till in up‐ice till plains. These large lodge moraines are thought to form by advection of subglacial till to a somewhat stationary margin forming a wedge over time. However, smaller end moraines that fit the definition of lodge moraines are found in Iceland and Norway where frozen‐on slabs of subglacial till are stacked at the margin during seasonal oscillations. Part of our rationale for this paper is pedagogical, in that a review shows that six of the most widely used glacial geology textbooks neither mention lodge moraines nor describe the till advection, wedge‐forming process that makes the large lodge moraines. We conclude that lodge moraines are common and of equal importance for understanding end‐moraine genesis as push, dump and hummocky end moraines.</jats:p>
items.summary: 《冰碛垄：一种常见但被低估的终碛类型——综述》：该文以成因分类梳理终碛，重点评述由冰下冰碛物在冰缘附近沉积而成的冰碛垄，指出其规模可达十公里以上、常见于劳伦泰德冰盖南缘及冰岛和斯堪的纳维亚，并强调六部常用冰川地质教材均未提及此类终碛，适合关注冰川地貌与终碛成因的读者了解这一被忽视的类型。
items.title: Lodge moraines: a common yet underreported end‐moraine type—a review

<jats:title>ABSTRACT</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Ancient settlement conditions on floodplains within the western part of the East European Plain remain obscure due to the limited archaeological and environmental research. This study presents a multidisciplinary geoarchaeological investigation of the Ostriv Dubovets site in northwestern Ukraine, including geomorphological, stratigraphic, micromorphological, particle size and magnetic susceptibility analyses. The site's pedosedimentary archive reveals a bipartite Late Glacial palaeosol, the upper of which shows signs of clay illuviation and cryogenic alteration. The periglacial phenomena are the youngest in this region, representing cryoturbation, cryogenic‐induced subsidence and frost fissures. Aeolian sand sedimentation during the Younger Dryas stadial led to the formation of an elevation that was inhabited by ancient people in the Mesolithic period. The site underwent strong soil redeposition and deflation until the onset of the Subatlantic period, when modern soil began to form. Both erosional and pedogenic phases were mainly governed by natural factors and land use practices, leading to multiple artefacts' redeposition. The study, for the first time in NW Ukraine, demonstrates the value of integrated geoarchaeological approaches for interpreting floodplain archives.</jats:p>

items.abstract: <jats:p>Numerous studies have shown that during the Quaternary there were substantial fluctuations in sea level in response to glacial–interglacial climate variability, reaching lowstand positions up to 134 m below the present sea level (b.s.l.). These fluctuations have had a strong influence on the morphology of shallow shelf seas, which preserve evidence of former terrestrial and coastal landscapes that are now submerged. Geomorphic analyses of submerged coastal landforms, such as marine terraces and clinothems, can thus provide valuable information regarding palaeoshoreline positions and insights into past sea levels. In this study, using high‐resolution acoustic methods, we investigated the Žirje Archipelago located along the central part of the karstified eastern Adriatic coast to detect the distribution and characteristics of submerged palaeoshorelines. The acquired data revealed a series of marine terraces at depths between 44.5 and 207.9 m b.s.l. Comparisons with available sea‐level curves show that these terraces formed during periods of sea‐level stillstands or decelerated rates of sea‐level rise, extending back to at least Marine Isotope Stage 10. In addition, progradational shelf‐edge delta clinoforms with rollover points at depths ranging from 127 to 131 m b.s.l. indicate the position of the shoreline during the Last Glacial Maximum (LGM). These features, observed on the slope towards the Mid‐Adriatic Deep, are interpreted as a lowstand wedge of the Late Pleistocene Krka River. By integrating information on erosional marine terraces and depositional clinothems, we propose new constraints on the evolution of Quaternary shorelines and variability in regional relative sea levels. Moreover, for the first time, we tentatively identify the position of the palaeoshoreline along the eastern Adriatic during the LGM. The surveyed area proved to be a natural laboratory for studying shelf‐edge environments adjacent to sediment‐starved karstified coasts.</jats:p>
